parsed.analysis: The review describes connection failures and resulting loss of rewards and VIP time, but explicitly attributes these behaviors to technical issues and connection problems. Under R11, malfunction-attributed behavior is not codable. "rare down time" describes when the reviewer plays, not a game-imposed schedule, and spending money is not linked to progress or a defined recurring-fee mechanic. No applicable label remains.

The review describes progression as available only through being rich or spending money, which satisfies Pay to Progress. It does not describe repetitive tasks, a specific currency conversion, purchased items losing value over time, or a competition mechanic. General difficulty, high costs, and complaints about customer support are not codable under R2.

labels.rationale: The span states that spending money is the only way to level up, making payment necessary for progression.

parsed.analysis: The review describes purchasing in-game coins with real money and paying to participate in a chance-based wheel, so M_IntermediateCurrency and M_Gambling are candidates. The missing 300 coins and omitted extras are explicitly attributed to a failure to receive the purchase, so R11 suppresses labels based on that malfunction; M_WasteAversion is therefore rejected.

labels.label: M_IntermediateCurrency
labels.span: I paid for 300 coins
labels.rationale: The reviewer describes exchanging real money for in-game coins.

labels.label: M_Gambling
labels.span: paid again to spin a wheel. got 2x on the wheel
labels.rationale: The reviewer describes paying to participate in a wheel-based chance mechanic with a variable reward.

parsed.analysis: The review describes spending as necessary for meaningful growth, satisfying Pay to Progress. It also describes the removal of player-versus-player play, but Competition requires competition to be present in the game, so it is not assigned. The statement that money was wasted does not specifically describe an acquired item losing value over time, so Power Creep is rejected; no other label has a qualifying mechanic span.

labels.label: M_PayToProgress
labels.span: You have to spend to have any meaningful growth
labels.rationale: The reviewer states that spending money is required for meaningful in-game progression.

parsed.analysis: The review describes older characters losing effectiveness as newer meta shifts occur, which is Power Creep. It also names the gacha pity mechanic, so Reward Mania applies. The statement about investing time and effort does not say that leaving is difficult, so Easy to Get Hard to Lose is rejected under its boundary rule. Low rewards and expensive or premium team compositions do not explicitly describe real-money payment enabling progress, so Pay to Progress, Gambling, and Intermediate Currency are rejected.

labels.label: M_PowerCreep
labels.span: old characters started falling off
labels.rationale: This describes previously acquired characters losing value or effectiveness as the game's meta changes.

labels.label: P_RewardMania
labels.span: barely gives us enough to hit hard pity
labels.rationale: “Hard pity” names a gacha draw mechanic whose reward-delivery structure sustains engagement.

parsed.analysis: The review describes team-based competition and matchmaking that places more skilled players on the enemy team than on the reviewer's team. This supports S_Competition and P_IllusionOfControl because the matchmaking is alleged to be unfairly arranged. No temporal, monetary, advertisement, social, collection, or technical mechanic is described; general anger and the recommendation not to play are not codable under R2.

labels.label: S_Competition
labels.span: in enemy team all of them will now how to play how to push when to engage and everything but in your team you will players with no game sense
labels.rationale: The span describes players being placed into opposing teams and competing against one another.

labels.label: P_IllusionOfControl
labels.span: unfair matchmaking
labels.rationale: The span asserts that matchmaking determines or arranges opponents and teammates unfairly, consistent with manipulated matchmaking outcomes.

parsed.analysis: The review describes purchased Poké Balls being consumed more quickly because Pokémon break out, followed by the claim that the player must purchase more to continue capturing. This supports Pay to Progress. Intermediate Currency is rejected because Poké Balls are items, not a described real-money-to-currency conversion; Gambling is rejected because no explicit real-money stake or gambling mechanic is described; Waste Aversion and Illusion of Control are rejected because no stranded value or asserted rigging is stated. The appended text says the reviewer did not write the review and did not speak to the players mentioned, indicating a review was posted or authored under the player's identity, so Friend Spam / Impersonation applies under R13.

labels.label: M_PayToProgress
labels.span: so I have to purchase more
labels.rationale: The player describes payment as necessary to replenish the items needed to continue making captures.

labels.label: S_FriendSpamImpersonation
labels.span: I DID NOT WRITE THIS REVIEW
labels.rationale: The span indicates that content was published as the player's store-review identity without their authorship.

M_EasyToPurchase is rejected because the review does not clearly describe an accidental purchase or a purchase prompt triggered by insufficient funds.

parsed.analysis: The review describes variable or chance-based rewards from chests and card rewards, supporting Reward Mania. Overpriced bundles do not establish a purchase-friction or scarcity mechanic; duplicated cards do not by themselves establish a compulsion to complete a collection; and the screens after running out of spins are not explicitly purchase prompts. Bots in clan chat describe other actors, not a game design mechanic.

parsed.analysis: The review describes a pay-to-win structure, base upgrade timers that impose waiting, and endlessly scaling progression with no clear endpoint. These support M_PayToProgress, T_PlayingByAppointment, and T_InfiniteTreadmill. I rejected T_Grinding because “just more grind” is a general evaluation without naming a repetitive activity tied to progress. I rejected M_UIMisdirection and M_EasyToPurchase because confusing and overwhelming UI is not enough to establish attention-steering, default purchasing, or an insufficient-funds prompt. I rejected S_ForcedFellowship and S_EncouragesAntiSocialBehavior because alliance pressure and attacks do not clearly describe recruitment obligation or a reward flowing from harmful conduct. S_Competition applies because the game places players in conflict through attacks.

labels.span: it's set up in a pay to win way
labels.rationale: This explicitly describes spending money as a route to an in-game advantage.

labels.label: T_PlayingByAppointment

labels.rationale: Base update times describe in-game timers that impose waits before progress can continue.

labels.label: T_InfiniteTreadmill
labels.span: Everything scales endlessly, there is kinda no point to look forward to
labels.rationale: Endless scaling and no meaningful endpoint describe progression that continually extends without completion.

labels.label: S_Competition
labels.span: If you are not in one then you get attacked and bullied
labels.rationale: This describes the game placing players in conflict through attacks by other players.

The event ranking also describes competition, supporting S_Competition. The dice shortage and logging in after 8 hours do not clearly describe an explicit timer, regeneration schedule, or required appointment, so T_PlayingByAppointment is rejected under its boundary rule. The refer-a-friend feature is reported as malfunctioning and no recruitment incentive is described, so no social label applies; the support failure itself is not codable under R11.

parsed.analysis: The review describes a maintenance/login malfunction that prevented access and caused troops and resources to be lost; under R11, the fault-attributed behavior is not codable. The two-hour login attempt is also a technical failure, not a designed wait timer or cooldown, so T_PlayingByAppointment is rejected. The long play history and deleted app do not show accumulated investment making departure difficult, so P_EasyToGetHardToLose is rejected.

The review describes limited board/storage capacity and a paid storage expansion whose price increases with each purchase. M_WasteAversion applies because finite capacity forces the player toward upgrading storage. M_IntermediateCurrency is rejected because the review does not describe real money being converted into diamonds. M_PayToProgress is rejected because the storage restriction is not explicitly described as blocking continued play or progress. T_Grinding is rejected because spending energy to obtain needed items does not clearly describe repetitive task performance.

labels.label: M_WasteAversion
labels.span: The limited space is bothersome too and you have to use diamonds to buy more storage with each purchase the price gets higher.
labels.rationale: Limited capacity forces the player to purchase additional storage, matching the capped-inventory/upgrade-storage indicator.

parsed.analysis: The review describes repetitive play to collect photos and complete a set, supporting T_Grinding and P_CompleteTheCollection. The extra-coin offer is payment for a collection item, but the review does not clearly establish real money being converted into coins or that payment is required for general progress, so M_IntermediateCurrency and M_PayToProgress are rejected. The missing promised photo is a failure to deliver, not a described chance mechanic, currency mismatch, or explicit bug, so M_Gambling, M_WasteAversion, and P_IllusionOfControl are rejected. No unreachable end state is established for T_InfiniteTreadmill.
